title: Ramayana: Part One opens across India with more than Rs 100 crore in advance sales
dek: Nitesh Tiwari's two-part epic released on Thursday in six languages with a 'U' certificate and a running time of 3 hours 15 minutes. Trackers say first-day bookings alone passed Rs 41 crore.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Ramayana: Part One, director Nitesh Tiwari's retelling of the epic and one of the most expensive Indian films ever made, opened in cinemas on Thursday, 5 November. Advance ticket sales across its first five days passed Rs 104 crore in India, including blocked seats, according to figures from the tracker Sacnilk reported by ETV Bharat.

The first shows in Mumbai were listed from 6 am on Thursday, according to ticketing listings reported by Flickonclick. The film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana.

## The film

The Central Board of Film Certification has given the Hindi version a "U" certificate, meaning it is cleared for all audiences, with a running time of 195 minutes, WION reported, citing the board's website. It is released in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and English, and in 2D, 3D, IMAX 3D, 4DX and ScreenX formats.

The cast also includes Ravie Dubey as Lakshmana, Sunny Deol as Hanuman, Arun Govil as Dasharatha, Lara Dutta as Kaikeyi and Rakul Preet Singh as Surpanakha. The music is by A R Rahman and Hans Zimmer. Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios produced it with Yash's Monster Mind Creations. The film is the first of two parts. In a court filing earlier this week, the budget for Part One was put at Rs 2,000 crore, Bar and Bench reported.

## Advance bookings

Sacnilk's figures, as reported by ETV Bharat, show 27.69 lakh tickets sold across 87,881 shows for the first five days, worth Rs 104.58 crore including blocked seats, or Rs 83.44 crore without them. Opening day accounted for Rs 41.21 crore.

Hindi brought in most of the money, at Rs 85.37 crore, followed by Telugu (Rs 8.57 crore), Kannada (Rs 7.86 crore), Tamil (Rs 2.23 crore) and Malayalam (about Rs 55 lakh). Overseas pre-sales were close to $3 million, about $2.15 million of it from North America.

Kamal Gianchandani of PVR INOX, India's largest multiplex chain, told ETV Bharat that the film could record the biggest pre-Diwali advance bookings in the chain's history of more than 30 years, with over Rs 25 crore in net advance sales across its screens.

These are trackers' and exhibitors' figures; the producers have not published their own. Advance totals also count only tickets bought before release, and differ between trackers depending on how blocked seats are treated.

## What to expect

Trade estimates cited by ETV Bharat put the likely first-day takings in India at about Rs 80 crore net, and the worldwide opening at Rs 150 to 160 crore gross. The film arrives three days before Diwali, on 8 November, a holiday period that usually brings big audiences, and after an October in which Indian films earned more than Rs 1,000 crore at the domestic box office.

Earlier this week the Bombay High Court granted the producer a "dynamic" injunction against piracy, which requires internet providers to block infringing links once they are notified, without fresh court orders. Opening-day figures from trackers are expected on Friday morning.
